questions.question: In which city is the Colosseum?
questions.fact: The Colosseum could hold around 50,000 spectators, and it opened in the year 80 with 100 days of games.

questions.question: In which city is the Taj Mahal?
questions.fact: Emperor Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal as a tomb for his beloved wife, Mumtaz Mahal. It took about 20 years.

questions.question: The Christ the Redeemer statue looks over which city?
questions.fact: Christ the Redeemer is about 30 metres tall and was finished in 1931. Its arms stretch about 28 metres wide.

questions.question: Where is the famous Leaning Tower?
questions.fact: The tower started leaning while it was still being built in the 1100s, because of soft ground.

questions.question: In which city is Big Ben?
questions.fact: Big Ben is really the name of the great bell. The tower was renamed the Elizabeth Tower in 2012.

questions.question: In which city is the Acropolis?
questions.fact: The Parthenon on the Acropolis is around 2,500 years old and was built for the goddess Athena.

questions.question: Which city has the Golden Gate Bridge?
questions.fact: The Golden Gate Bridge opened in 1937. Its famous colour is called "International Orange".

questions.question: The Sydney Opera House is in which country?
questions.fact: The Sydney Opera House was designed by Danish architect Jørn Utzon, who never saw it finished.

questions.question: Petra, the city carved into pink rock, is in which country?
questions.fact: Petra was built by the Nabataeans over 2,000 years ago. It featured in "Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade".

questions.question: Angkor Wat is in which country?
questions.fact: Angkor Wat is the largest religious monument in the world, and it even appears on Cambodia's flag.

questions.question: In which country are the Maya ruins of Chichén Itzá?
questions.fact: At the spring and autumn equinoxes, shadows make a "serpent" seem to slither down Chichén Itzá's main pyramid.

questions.question: Which city has the Brandenburg Gate?
questions.fact: The Brandenburg Gate stood right by the Berlin Wall, and became a symbol of Germany's reunion in 1989–90.

questions.question: The Little Mermaid statue is in which city?
questions.fact: The Little Mermaid statue is only about 1.25 metres tall, smaller than many visitors expect.

questions.question: Which city is famous for canals and gondolas?
questions.fact: Venice is built on over 100 small islands, connected by around 400 bridges.

questions.question: The Atomium is a landmark in which city?
questions.fact: The Atomium was built for the 1958 World's Fair and shows an iron crystal magnified 165 billion times.

questions.question: Neuschwanstein Castle, which inspired Disney, is in which country?
questions.fact: Neuschwanstein was built by King Ludwig II of Bavaria, who died before it was finished.

questions.question: Mont-Saint-Michel, the island abbey, is in which country?
questions.fact: At high tide, Mont-Saint-Michel becomes an island. The tides in its bay are among the strongest in Europe.

questions.question: Which city has the medieval Charles Bridge?
questions.fact: Charles Bridge was started in 1357 and is lined with 30 statues of saints.

questions.question: The Hagia Sophia is in which city?
questions.fact: The Hagia Sophia was built in 537 as a church, became a mosque, then a museum, and is a mosque again today.

questions.question: What is the tallest mountain in Africa?
questions.fact: Kilimanjaro is 5,895 m high, and you can climb it without technical climbing gear.

questions.question: Table Mountain looks over which city?
questions.fact: Table Mountain has a flat top about 3 km wide, often covered by a cloud called "the tablecloth".

questions.question: Niagara Falls are on the border between the USA and…
questions.fact: Niagara Falls are made of three waterfalls. The biggest, Horseshoe Falls, is mostly in Canada.

questions.question: What is the tallest waterfall in the world?
questions.fact: Angel Falls in Venezuela drops 979 m, nearly 20 times the height of Niagara Falls.

questions.question: Iguazu Falls are on the border of Argentina and…
questions.fact: Iguazu has around 275 separate waterfalls. The biggest is called the Devil's Throat.

questions.question: Victoria Falls are on the border of Zambia and…
questions.fact: Locals call Victoria Falls "Mosi-oa-Tunya", meaning "the smoke that thunders".

questions.question: Which city has the Burj Khalifa, the world's tallest building?
questions.fact: The Burj Khalifa is about 828 m tall. On a clear day you can see it from around 95 km away.

questions.question: Where is the Forbidden City?
questions.fact: The Forbidden City was home to Chinese emperors for about 500 years. Ordinary people weren't allowed in.

questions.question: Mount Fuji is in which country?
questions.fact: Mount Fuji is an active volcano. It last erupted in 1707.

questions.question: Times Square is in which city?
questions.fact: Times Square is named after The New York Times, which moved there in 1904. About a million people watch the ball drop on New Year's Eve.

questions.question: The Statue of Liberty stands in which city's harbour?
questions.fact: The Statue of Liberty was a gift from France in 1886. Its inside frame was designed by Gustave Eiffel.

questions.question: Which US national park has the "Old Faithful" geyser?
questions.fact: Old Faithful erupts about every 60 to 110 minutes. Yellowstone was the world's first national park, in 1872.

questions.question: Which river carved the Grand Canyon?
questions.fact: The Grand Canyon is up to about 1.8 km deep, and its oldest rocks are almost 2 billion years old.

questions.question: Stonehenge is in which country?
questions.fact: Some of Stonehenge's smaller stones were brought from Wales, about 250 km away, around 5,000 years ago.

questions.question: What are the giant stone heads on Easter Island called?
questions.fact: There are nearly 1,000 moai. Many have bodies buried underground, not just heads.

questions.question: Easter Island belongs to which country?
questions.fact: Easter Island is about 3,500 km off the coast of Chile, one of the most remote inhabited islands on Earth.

questions.question: The Galápagos Islands belong to which country?
questions.fact: Darwin's visit to the Galápagos in 1835 helped inspire his theory of evolution.

questions.question: Which Portuguese city is famous for port wine and the Dom Luís I bridge?
questions.fact: The Dom Luís I bridge was designed by a former partner of Gustave Eiffel and opened in 1886.

questions.question: Which tower guarded the river Tagus in Lisbon?
questions.fact: Belém Tower was built in the 1500s, in the age when Portuguese explorers sailed from Lisbon.

questions.question: The Tower of Hercules, the oldest working Roman lighthouse, is in which city?
questions.fact: The Tower of Hercules is almost 2,000 years old and still works as a lighthouse today.

questions.question: Which grand palace near Paris was built for Louis XIV?
questions.fact: Versailles's Hall of Mirrors has 357 mirrors. The treaty ending World War I was signed there in 1919.

questions.question: The Matterhorn sits on the border of Switzerland and…
questions.fact: The Matterhorn is about 4,478 m high, and it's said to have inspired the shape of Toblerone bars.

questions.question: Which city's cathedral has Brunelleschi's famous dome?
questions.fact: Brunelleschi's dome, finished in the 1430s, is still the largest brick dome ever built.

questions.question: The Trevi Fountain is in which city?
questions.fact: People throw around €3,000 in coins into the Trevi Fountain every day. The money goes to charity.

questions.question: Which city has a famous Parliament building on the Danube?
questions.fact: Hungary's Parliament is one of the largest buildings in Europe and is especially stunning lit up at night.

questions.question: The Kremlin and Red Square are in which city?
questions.fact: "Red Square" didn't get its name from communism: the old Russian word "krasnaya" meant both "red" and "beautiful".

questions.question: The Great Pyramid of Giza is near which city?
questions.fact: The Great Pyramid was the tallest building on Earth for nearly 4,000 years, and it's the only ancient Wonder still standing.

questions.question: Where is the famous Blue Lagoon geothermal spa?
questions.fact: The Blue Lagoon's water gets its milky blue colour from silica, and it's warm all year round, about 37 to 40 °C.

questions.question: Which Greek island is famous for white houses with blue domes?
questions.fact: Santorini's island shape comes from a huge volcanic eruption about 3,600 years ago.

questions.question: Where in Europe can you most easily see the Northern Lights?
questions.fact: The best time to see the Northern Lights is on dark, clear nights from about September to March.

questions.question: Which German city has a giant twin-spired Gothic cathedral by the Rhine?
questions.fact: Cologne Cathedral took over 600 years to finish, from 1248 to 1880.

questions.question: Bruges, famous for canals and chocolate, is in which country?
questions.fact: Bruges's medieval centre is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and it's often called "the Venice of the North".

questions.question: What is Madrid's main airport called?
questions.fact: Madrid's airport was renamed in 2014 after Adolfo Suárez, Spain's first democratically elected Prime Minister after Franco.

questions.question: What is Barcelona's main airport called?
questions.fact: Barcelona's airport is officially named after Josep Tarradellas, a former president of Catalonia.

questions.question: Ha Long Bay, with its limestone islands, is in which country?
questions.fact: Ha Long means "descending dragon". Legend says dragons created its islands to protect Vietnam.

questions.question: Bali is an island in which country?
questions.fact: Indonesia has over 17,000 islands. Bali is known as the "Island of the Gods".

questions.question: The Maldives are in which ocean?
questions.fact: The Maldives are the world's lowest-lying country, on average only about 1.5 m above sea level.

questions.question: Which Los Angeles street has the Walk of Fame stars in its pavement?
questions.fact: The Hollywood Walk of Fame has more than 2,700 stars. Some, like Mickey Mouse, belong to cartoon characters.

questions.question: Which city is called "the City of Light"?
questions.fact: Paris is called "the City of Light" partly because it was one of the first cities with widespread street lighting.

questions.question: Which city is known as "the Eternal City"?
questions.fact: Rome is called "the Eternal City" because ancient Romans believed it would last forever.

questions.question: Which bell tower in Seville was once a minaret?
questions.fact: La Giralda is about 100 m tall. Instead of stairs, it has 35 ramps so guards could ride up on horseback.

questions.question: The Plaza de España with colourful tiled alcoves for every province is in which city?
questions.fact: Seville's Plaza de España was built for the 1929 Ibero-American Exposition and appears in Star Wars films.

questions.question: Which famous street market is held every Sunday in Madrid?
questions.fact: El Rastro has been held for over 250 years, around the Ribera de Curtidores street in La Latina.

questions.question: Barcelona's famous food market on La Rambla is called…
questions.fact: La Boqueria's history goes back to the 1200s, when traders sold meat at the city gates.
